title: Same genus or mere homonym? — a philosophical quarrel, not a theological one
source_text: LXXXII. Veruntamen inter se disceptant iidem Reformati, An fides historica & justificans sint species comprehensae sub eodem genere, aut univoco, aut saltem analogo; an vero solum vocis homonymae diversae acceptiones? Sed hanc quaestionem putamus esse mere Philosophicam: Et modo constet qua in re inter se differant fides historica atque justificans, Theologiae nihil interesse qua voce Philosophica discrimen illud designetur. Si tamen volumus uti vocibus Philosophicis secundum morem in Scholis usitatum, non video quid obstet, quominus fides historica & justificans dicantur species ejusdem generis; cum non tantum utrique sit nomen quoddam commune, sed etiam id quoddam per nomen significatum; quandoquidem utraque est assensus quidam Deo revelanti adhibitus, ex Spiritus Sancti illuminatione.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless the same Reformers dispute among themselves whether historical and justifying faith are species comprehended under the same genus, either univocal or at least analogical; or whether they are only diverse acceptations of a homonymous word. But we think this question is merely Philosophical: and provided it is settled in what respect historical and justifying faith differ from each other, it is of no interest to Theology by what Philosophical word that difference is designated. Yet if we wish to use Philosophical words according to the custom usual in the Schools, I do not see what prevents historical and justifying faith from being called species of the same genus; since not only is there a certain common name for both, but also a certain thing signified by the name; inasmuch as each is a certain assent given to God revealing, from the illumination of the Holy Spirit.
pass_b_english: Reformers quarrel: are historical and justifying faith species under one genus (univocal or analogical), or only homonyms?
Le Blanc: the question is merely philosophical — once the real difference is clear, Theology need not care which school-word names it.
If we keep school usage: nothing blocks calling them species of one genus — common name and common thing: assent to God revealing, from the Spirit’s light.

lemmas.gloss: that this question is merely Philosophical

choices.term: Theologiae nihil interesse qua voce Philosophica discrimen illud designetur
choices.english: it is of no interest to Theology by what Philosophical word that difference is designated
choices.why: Le Blanc brackets the genus/homonym dispute.
rejected: Theology hangs on settling univocity vs homonymy first
